requirements.verified_by: read ARCHITECTURE.md and tinydb/table.py diff (2 lines, Table.update/Table.remove only)

findings.problem: Applying document_id_class() to every requested ID truncates non-integral floats, so a float ID silently updates the wrong document (int(1.5) == 1). On main the same call was a no-op.
Same conversion in remove(): a float ID such as 1.5 removes document 1 instead of being skipped, risking deletion of the wrong record.
findings.evidence: int(1.5) == 1 in Python; PR remove(doc_ids=[1.5]) resolves to doc_id 1 while origin/main skipped it

findings.problem: Non-numeric strings now raise ValueError instead of being skipped, contradicting the issue ('IDs that don't exist should still just be skipped like today') and get()'s semantics; the docstring still promises silent skipping.
findings.evidence: probe: get(doc_ids=['abc']) -> []; update(doc_ids=['abc']) -> ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'abc'; docstring at tinydb/table.py:437-440 says 'IDs that don't refer to an existing document are silently skipped'

findings.problem: Type hints and docstrings for update()/remove() still declare doc_ids as Iterable[int] and do not mention string-ID support; no docs/changelog.rst entry was added for the behaviour change.
findings.evidence: git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat shows only tests/test_autose_issue_2.py and tinydb/table.py changed; docs/changelog.rst has no entry for this fix

summary: The core string-ID conversion is the right mechanism and passes the suite, but applying document_id_class() to every ID truncates floats so the wrong document is updated/removed, and non-numeric strings now raise instead of being skipped as the issue requires.
